subject.title: perf: use a focused OpenClaw prepack profile for diagnostics

question: Should Kova diagnostics use a new supported focused OpenClaw prepack profile, and which package contents may it omit without invalidating release-shaped evidence?
rationale: The requested speedup changes the meaning of the packaged runtime and likely introduces cross-repository profile or configuration surface; source inspection alone cannot choose that product contract or benchmark threshold.

options.title: Define a supported diagnostics profile
options.body: Specify the allowed omissions and benchmark target in the packaging layer, then update Kova to request that profile with focused compatibility coverage.

options.title: Optimize generic packaging
options.body: Keep one release-shaped package contract and pursue caching or incremental packaging improvements that benefit diagnostics without a separate profile.

options.title: Decline the specialization
options.body: Keep the generic path if the measured savings do not justify another packaging mode and its maintenance burden.

recommendation.title: Define a supported diagnostics profile
recommendation.body: Specify the allowed omissions and benchmark target in the packaging layer, then update Kova to request that profile with focused compatibility coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: They own this issue and recently led the adjacent Kova performance work needed to define and measure the intended outcome.
